justification: Adds a deterministic, evidence-recording proof method for served state-law rows (rules 1-3) and a verifier that re-derives each proof from stored evidence alone. Read-only against the database; no write is applied by this change. The plan it produces proves 1 of 630 candidate rows, which is the honest yield: 525 rows are not contiguous in the in-force law at all (paraphrase / stale), and the method fails closed on ambiguity.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_state_law_evidence.py -q && python scripts/verify_state_law_evidence.py data/state_law_evidence_2026-10-17.jsonl
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A matcher accepts a row it should refuse. Six mutations were injected and measured: word-boundary check removed (1 test fails), several-occurrence guard removed (3 fail), rule 3 single-result guards loosened (1 fail each), minimum-words guard removed (1 fails). One mutant survives by design: allowing a 1-unit tile in rule 2, which is unreachable because rule 1 claims every single-unit span first. The verifier exits 1 on tampered offsets, row text, unit id, snapshot hash or version.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The pinned legislation.nsw.gov.au snapshots (sha256 in data/law_text_cache/manifest.json, identical to the files used by passes 1-3). The verifier reloads them by hash and compares the stored offsets to the law's own text.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Injected 6 mutations into scripts/state_law_evidence.py and ran tests/test_state_law_evidence.py: word-boundary check removed -> 1 failed; several-occurrence guard removed -> 3 failed; rule 3 single-result guards loosened -> 1 failed each; min-words guard removed -> 1 failed. Restored: 22 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: scripts/state_law_proof.py, state_law_proof2.py, state_law_recopy.py and apply_state_law_proof.py (read in full); skipped reasons in data/state_law_recopy_skipped_2026-10-16.csv. regulatory_provisions has no evidence column, so evidence is a committed JSONL keyed by id + text md5.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed old PDFs would be in R2 for rule 3. Only page PNGs exist (pdf-pages/sepp-*), no PDF text, so rule 3 is implemented and tested but returns no_old_pdf for the 3 ambiguous rows. Also assumed the snapshots were fetched by the Fly app; its DNS is down, so they were copied from sibling worktrees and their sha256 matched the manifest.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: New matcher module with one exact test per rule instead of the 90% word-run share in the recopy pass; reuses the unit classes, snapshot cache, manifest and candidate query.

functions.name: prove
functions.input: a snapshot and the normalised row text
functions.output: proven (rule 1 or 2, with unit ids and offsets), ambiguous (several occurrences) or unproven with a reason
functions.if_none: an empty or short row returns unproven too_short; never proven

values.value: 630 candidates: 1 proven (rule 1), 525 not contiguous in instrument, 60 unmapped instrument, 32 too short, 9 inside no unit, 3 ambiguous (no old PDF)
values.read_at: python scripts/state_law_proof4.py --date 2026-10-17 against the read-only database, 2026-10-17
values.if_missing: the yield claim would be unsupported

queries.purpose: Candidate rows: served state-law rules not yet proven, with the old PDF page and file for rule 3
queries.where_clause: is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND provision type not TOC AND source_council IS NULL AND NOT (citation_status IN proven/imprecise OR page_check IN on_page/moved)

break_it.scenario: A row that repeats inside one unit, or occurs in two parts, is silently proven against the first hit.
break_it.what_happens: It is reported ambiguous or unproven; tests test_rule1_repeat_in_two_units_is_ambiguous_not_proven and test_rule3_refuses_when_the_part_itself_repeats_the_text fail if that guard is removed.
break_it.how: Mutation of the guards was run; the tests go red.

break_it.scenario: A row ends before the law's full stop, or begins mid-word.
break_it.what_happens: A trailing full stop is accepted (word_aligned); a mid-word start or end is refused.
break_it.how: test_rule1_refuses_row_that_starts_mid_word; mutation removing the check fails a test.

break_it.scenario: Someone edits an evidence record (offsets, row text, unit id, snapshot hash, version) so a false proof is applied.
break_it.what_happens: verify_state_law_evidence.py exits 1; apply_state_law_proof.py refuses the plan because check_evidence re-verifies every row.
break_it.how: Verifier tests tamper each field and expect a failure reason.

break_it.scenario: Candidate rows: served state-law rules not yet proven are missed or over-included because the query filter is wrong (for example a row already proven is proposed again, or a council row slips in).
break_it.what_happens: A missed row is only a missed opportunity; an over-included row is still refused unless its text is a contiguous span of the law, and apply_state_law_proof.py re-checks is_current, source_council IS NULL and the text md5 before any write.
break_it.how: The query is the pass 1 CANDIDATES_SQL unchanged apart from two extra selected columns; the runner is read-only.

residual_risk: Snapshots are gitignored, so CI can only run the verifier against a cache that has them; the unit tests use synthetic HTML and need nothing. Rule 3 cannot fire until an old PDF with a text layer is supplied via --pdf-dir. Rows whose text lies partly outside any id'd unit (9) stay unproven.

post_merge.db_reset: none -- nothing is written to the database by this change
post_merge.secrets: none added; the runner reads DATABASE_URL read-only as passes 1-3 do
post_merge.manual_verify: With the snapshots cached, run python scripts/verify_state_law_evidence.py data/state_law_evidence_2026-10-17.jsonl --db and expect 1 verified; applying the plan is a separate decision.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/apply_state_law_proof.py: check_evidence reads a JSONL file and the pinned snapshots, no database or HTTP call; the existing database write path is unchanged and still dry-run by default.
real_layer_exempt.scripts/state_law_proof4.py: Read-only database session (default_transaction_read_only=on) used only to fetch candidate rows; every decision is made by pure functions (state_law_evidence.py) that tests/test_state_law_evidence.py exercises on synthetic HTML, and the final result is checked against the real pinned law snapshots by verify_state_law_evidence.py. No write path is added.
real_layer_exempt.scripts/verify_state_law_evidence.py: The optional --db flag runs one read-only SELECT of md5(provision_text); the verification itself is database-free and run against the real snapshots on 2026-10-17 (1 of 1 verified).
